function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide showing **exactly** how you can pull data for a specific interface from your fabric using the `telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get` helper. Feel free to copy/paste it into a Jupyter notebook, VS Code terminal, or whatever environment runs plain Python 3. --- ### 1️⃣ What You Need To Know First | Parameter | Meaning | Example | |-----------|---------|--------| | `fabricName` | Name/label of the fabric you’re querying (e.g., `"core-fabric"`). | `"core-fabric"` | | `nodeId` | Integer ID of the switch/node inside that fabric. | `1012` | | `podId` | Integer ID of the pod where the node lives. | `5` | | `interfaceType` | Type of interface you care about.
Options:
  • `"svi"` – Switch Virtual Interface
  • `"ethernet"` – Physical Ethernet port
  • `"loopback"` – Loopback address/interface
  • `"port-channel"` – Aggregated link group
| `"ethernet"` | | `infoType` | Kind of detail you want back.
Options:
  • `"interfaces"` – Basic config & attributes
  • `"status"` – Operational state (up/down)
  • `"statistics"` – Traffic counters
  • `"errors"` – Error counts / alarms
| `"statistics"` | If you don’t know one of those values yet, start by running a *list* query first (most APIs expose something like `/fabrics/{name}/nodes`). Once you’ve got the IDs, plug them in below. --- ### 2️⃣ One‑liner Call (Python) ```python from functions import telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get result = telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get( fabricName="core-fabric", # <-- change this! nodeId=1012, # <-- change this! podId=5, # <-- change this! interfaceType="ethernet", # <-- pick one of svi/ethernet/loopback/port-channel infoType="statistics" # <-- pick one of interfaces/status/statistics/errors ) print(result) # Pretty‑printed JSON will appear ``` That’s all there is to it! The returned object (`result`) will contain exactly the fields requested: ```json { "interface": { "id": "Ethernet0/48", "description": "Uplink to Spine A", ... }, "statistics": { "in_octets": 123456789, "out_octets": 987654321, "in_errors": 12, "out_errors": 7, ... } } ``` *(Actual keys depend on the underlying platform.)* --- ### 3️⃣ Common Pitfalls & How to Fix Them | Symptom | Likely Cause | Quick Remedy | |---------|--------------|-------------| | Function throws “404 Not Found” | Fabric, node, or pod ID doesn’t exist | Double‑check spelling/case of `fabricName`; verify numeric IDs | | Empty result set | No matching interface of that type exists on the node | Try another `interfaceType`, e.g., `"svi"` instead of `"ethernet"` | | Unexpected field names | Platform version changed schema | Inspect raw payload (`print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))`) and adjust downstream parsing accordingly | | Permission denied | Your credentials lack read access to telemetry | Ask admin to grant `Telemetry.Read` role or similar | --- ### 4️⃣ Extending It: Pull All Interfaces at Once Sometimes you just want a list of *all* interfaces’ status before drilling down. Many platforms support a wildcard request—if yours does, replace the last two arguments with `"*"`. For instance: ```python all_statuses = telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get( fabricName="core-fabric", nodeId=1012, podId=5, interfaceType="*", # fetch both ethernet + svi + others infoType="status" ) for iface in all_statuses.get("interfaces", []): print(f"{iface['id']}: {iface['operStatus']} ({iface['adminState']})") ``` This gives you a quick health snapshot across the entire chassis. --- ### 5️⃣ Wrap‑Up Checklist ✅ [ ] Confirm you have the correct **Fabric**, **Node**, and **Pod** identifiers. ✅ [ ] Pick the right **Interface Type** for what you actually see on the device. ✅ [ ] Decide whether you need configuration, operational state, traffic stats, or error logs. ✅ [ ] Run the single line above and inspect the JSON. ✅ [ ] Handle pagination or rate limits if your fabric has thousands of interfaces (some APIs return paged responses). Happy monitoring! 🚀
